keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. The page names the capital and 'the adjacent cities of Bukan, Oshnavieh, Piranshahr and Naghadeh' and gives no area, so a radius of 80 km around Mahabad is the researcher's reading. The republic also claimed Urmia, Khoy and Salmas, held by the Azerbaijan People's Government.

ledger.note: 15 December 1945: the Kurdish People's Government is founded at Mahabad. 'On December 15, the Kurdish People's Government was founded in Mahabad' (the year implied by the page); the Iran crisis page: 'The Mahabad Republic was proclaimed in December 1945'. The infobox gives 'Autonomy declared: 22 January 1946' and calls it an 'Unrecognized puppet state of the Soviet Union'; the page contradicts itself on the date.

22 January 1946: Qazi Muhammad announces the Republic of Mahabad. 'On January 22, 1946, Qazi Muhammad announced the formation of the Republic of Mahabad.' The Soviets promised on 26 March 1946 to leave north-western Iran.

wars.outcome: Iranian victory: Soviet troops left on 6 May 1946 and Iranian forces entered Tabriz on 11 December and Mahabad on 15 December 1946, dissolving both republics.

certainty.note: A Kurdish enclave under Soviet cover; no page gives its boundary and it claimed three cities held by the Azerbaijan People's Government.

notes: Rebel state written by group me-10-h for the pahlavi-dynasty dossier (loss December 1945, gain December 1946). It held land for about a year. The Mahabad page contradicts itself on the founding (15 December 1945 for the Kurdish People's Government, 'not declared until December 1945', 22 January 1946 in the infobox) and gives 15 December 1946 for the end (the Iran crisis page: the Barzanis withdrew on 15 December 1946).
